newsitem.title: USA: Boehringer's combination inhaler available in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Boehringer's combination inhaler available in U.S.

text.p: Boehringer Ingelheim Corp said Thursday that its Combivent Inhalation Aerosol, a preparation that combines two widely prescribed medicines in a single, metered dose inhaler is now available to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), known collectively as chronic bronchitis and emphysema in the United States.

In a press release, the division of Germany's Boehringer Ingelheim said the product is indicated for use in patients with COPD on a regular aerosol bronchodilator who continue to have evidence of bronchospasm (spasmodic airway muscle contraction) and who require a second bronchodilator to widen, or dilate, constricted airways, or the tubes carrying air to the lungs.
Combivent combines albuterol sulfate, an off-patent drug, with ipratropium bromide, which is made by Boehringer.
A company spokesman that Combivent has annual sales of $41 milllion outside the United States.
